items.followUp: Differentiate between translatory and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining feature of rotatory motion.
rubric.description: States that rotatory motion is motion about an axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body rotates about an axis or that its points move in circular paths around the axis.

rubric.why: Distinguishes vibration by its back-and-forth motion around a central position.
rubric.description: States that vibratory motion is to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the motion as to and fro about a mean position.

modelAnswer: Rotatory motion: Motion of a body about an axis; its points move in circular paths around that axis.
Vibratory motion: To-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.

items.followUp: Define circular motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Explains that random motion is irregular and lacks a fixed path or direction.
rubric.description: Defines random motion as irregular motion without a fixed path or direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the motion as irregular and stating that it has no fixed path or direction.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of random motion.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of random motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as the random motion of gas molecules.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which an object moves irregularly, without a fixed path or direction.
Example: The random motion of gas molecules.

items.followUp: What is an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: States that a rigid body does not deform when a force is applied.
rubric.description: States that the shape and size of a rigid body remain unchanged when a force is applied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its shape and size do not change under an applied force.

rubric.why: Gives the defining condition that the body's points maintain fixed separation.
rubric.description: States that the distance between any two points of a rigid body remains constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the distance between any two points remains constant.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when a force is applied.
The distance between any two points of a rigid body remains constant.
